_note: Resident actions come ONLY from official pages read on 2026-10-29 (sources below). 'message_focus' is our analysis-based wording for the regional civil protection authority and is a DRAFT to validate. Where no source was read for a country, there is no action for that country.

bbk.name: BBK (Germany): Vorsorge und Handeln bei Hochwasser

rijks.name: Rijksoverheid (Netherlands): Wat moet ik doen bij een dreigende overstroming?

DE.text: Follow flood warnings via the NINA warning app, radio or the internet, and check current water levels with the state flood centres (hochwasserzentralen.de).

BE.text: Register on BE-Alert so you are warned even when you are outside the risk zone (up to 5 addresses, e.g. work or a vulnerable relative). On an alert, follow the instructions in the message.

NL.text: Keep your phone on (not in airplane or Do-not-disturb mode). NL-Alert needs no registration on most phones and tells you what is happening, what to do and where to find updates.

DE.text: Find out whether your home is in a flood or heavy-rain risk area: ask your municipality and check the state flood centres and municipal heavy-rain hazard maps.

NL.text: Prepare for a flood with Denk Vooruit (denkvooruit.nl); the government also points to overstroomik.nl for further information.

BE.text: Find out whether your area is flood-prone (zones sensibles) and keep gutters and ditches clean and clear.

DE.text: Make an emergency plan early: can sick or dependent people be evacuated in time and where to, pets, agreed signals with neighbours if phone networks fail, who does what. Keep your document folder and emergency bag ready; stock food, drinking water, a battery or crank radio and a flashlight.

NL.text: Prepare an emergency kit: medication, hygiene products, a first-aid kit, and enough non-perishable food and drinking water.

BE.text: Know where to cut the gas and electricity, and protect important papers and valuables from water (for example by keeping them up high).

DE.text: Get sandbags, stop boards and waterproof plywood; move valuable furniture and devices to protected upper rooms; keep hazardous substances out of the water's reach; secure the heating-oil tank against buoyancy; clear cellar rooms that can fill with water.

BE.text: Prepare sealing materials for the cellar hatch and sewer covers, raising materials (bricks or sandbags) for ground-floor and basement rooms, and boots, buckets and squeegees.
If told to shelter: go into the nearest building, close doors and windows and listen to the media. If told to evacuate: follow the instructions of the authorities and emergency services.

NL.text: When a flood threatens, decide whether to stay or leave depending on when it is expected, and follow your Veiligheidsregio and the regional disaster radio. If you stay: go to the highest place and turn off gas, water and electricity. If you leave: take only essentials, plan your route and transport, and tell family and friends where you are going.

DE.text: During a flood: do not stay in the cellar (it is life-threatening); switch off electrical devices and heating in rooms that could flood (risk of electric shock); do not drive through flooded roads and keep away from riverbanks; take children out of the flood area in time; follow the instructions and barriers of the emergency services. The BBK page does not cover evacuation or emergency numbers, so follow your local authorities.

BE.text: If someone's life is in danger, call 112. For other help from the fire service, use 1722.be (or call 1722 when that number is active). If you must evacuate, follow the instructions of the emergency services: close the main gas, electricity and water valves, lock doors and windows, and take spare clothes and boots.

1A.label: Priority: high exposure, flood mostly outside modelled hazard zones
1A.message_focus: Priority for alert-registration and preparedness messages. Say that this flood reached places the hazard maps do not show (less than 50% of the observed flood lies inside the EFAS 100-year zone), so residents should not rely on hazard maps alone.

1B.label: Priority: high exposure, known hazard zone
1B.message_focus: Priority for preparedness messages in an area already known as a hazard zone: make sure residents are registered for alerts, have a plan and a kit, and know what to do when told to shelter or evacuate.

2.label: Targeted: medium exposure
2.message_focus: Targeted reminders to register for alerts and to prepare a plan and kit.

3.label: Low observed exposure (mapped area)
3.message_focus: General alert-registration awareness. Low exposure was observed in the mapped part of this commune.

ND.label: No data: commune mostly outside the mapped areas
ND.message_focus: Exposure is unknown, not low: do not read grey as safe. The flood was not mapped here.
